issue.title: [var-log] files/sub-folder under /var/log folder missing because SONiC mount /var/log as a RAM disk/ext4 file.

failure.body:
#### Description
SONiC will mound a ram disk or ext4 to /var/log.
So when /var/log been remount, any data under this folder will lost.
Some service fordepends the folder structure under this folder, if the folder structure lost, server will break, for example auditd depends on /var/log/audit and if the folder lost, auditd can't startup.

#### Steps to reproduce the issue:
1. Install auditd, and create /var/log/audit in build_debian.sh
2. Build image.
3. Start a testbed VM with SONiC image in step4
4. Check /var/log, the /var/log/audit created in step1 will missing, auditd can't start.

#### Describe the results you received:
/var/log/audit missing after /var/log re-create.

#### Describe the results you expected:
/var/log/audit still exist after /var/log re-create.

resolution.title: [build_debian.sh]: Fix /var/log having 0750 permissions instead of 0755
resolution.description:
Fixes #9548 and #10015

Signed-off-by: Saikrishna Arcot <<EMAIL>>

#### Why I did it

PR #9481 changed auditd's log directory to be /var/log instead of
/var/log/audit, because SONiC mounts a disk image at /var/log during
runtime, and so the /var/log/audit directory might not exist (since it
would've been created during package installation, mounting another
partition at /var/log will hide it). However, for security reasons,
auditd changes the log directory to have 0750 permissions, so that not
everyone knows about the audit logs or read them.

This means that not even admin can list files in /var/log, which is a
regression from previous images.

#### How I did it

To fix this, revert the change to auditd's log directory, and tell
systemd to create the audit log directory at runtime if it doesn't
exist. Because the disk image gets mounted during initramfs (before
systemd starts), systemd will make sure that the /var/log/audit
directory will exist.

#### How to verify it

With this change, /var/log should have 0755 permissions, and admin should
be able to list the files in the directory.
